newsitem.title: FRANCE: French justice to probe Jewish wartime files find.
newsitem.headline: French justice to probe Jewish wartime files find.

text.p: A French official said on Friday he lodged a complaint against persons unknown for stealing public documents after files from a French wartime internment camp for Jews bound for Nazi death camps were found on a rubbish tip.

Bernard Bonnet, the prefect (government representative) in the southern town of Perpignan, also launched legal action for illegal possession of public documents against a town hall employee and a local journalist.

The employee, Yves Chamoux, has said he found the documents and was reported to have kept them for six months before handing them to journalist Joel Mettai at the local newspaper L'Independant de Perpignan.
The daily has said it kept the files for several more weeks in order to publish its report to coincide with the anniversary of Germany's World War Two surrender last May 8.
The newspaper has said the files included the names of about 1,000 Jews taken between April and December 1942 to and from the infamous Rivesaltes camp, in the foothills of the Pyrenees.

Some 2,000 Jews were deported from Rivesaltes to Drancy camp in the Paris suburbs which was run by the occupying German forces. From Drancy, internees were sent to Nazi death camps where most were killed on arrival in gas chambers.
The nature of the files remained unclear. Nazi hunter Serge Klarsfeld has said they appeared to be copies of documents he had consulted previously at the local archives.
The director of public archives, Marie-Edith de Lavergnee, has said all archives on World War Two internees in the region were in her possession and none had been stolen.

France's Jewish community has voiced outrage at such files being thrown onto a rubbish dump, but has said they could help clarify the responsibility of the wartime collaborationist Vichy government in the Holocaust ahead of the trial of former minister Maurice Papon.
Papon, 86, is to go on trial in October on charges of crimes against humanity for ordering the deportation of 1,560 Jews from southwest France to death camps.
